statement: For the curve, line bundles, fixed fourth-root isomorphism, and six vectors wj ∈ H0(Γ, Φ)∗ of Proposition 2.3, one can choose the basis u with unchanged determinant so that (u1)0 is an unramified fiber of f disjoint from Z. Set r = ξu and define v∗ j = ι∗ wj ∈ W∗ , V = 6 ∑ j=1 v∗ j . For any mutually disjoint compatible coordinate disks as above there are nonzero constants cj and a global pair P = (P1, P2) ∈ H0 (C, θ + Z)⊕2 with the following properties. First, cjlj = v∗ j , V 2 = 90 = 9 deg L, (v∗ j )2 + v∗ j · V = 1. (3.13) On disk j, using coefficient rows in the indicated frames, put mj = cj zj , Rj = mjr, Wj = Rj(0) ∧ R′ j(0), pj = P − mjr′ . (3.14) The pair P has principal part Rj(0)/zj in the frame (ℓfr j )2 of θ; the rows Rj, pj are holomorphic on the disk, and Rj(0) ̸= 0. Moreover, Wj = (v∗ j )2 , pj(0) ∧ Rj(0) = 1, 6 ∑ j=1 (Wj − 1) = −9 deg L. (3.15) Globally, J = u ∧ P ∈ H0 (C, Λ), ⟨[J], [T]⟩ = −V ([T]) for every T ∈ H0 (C, Λ). (3.16) Changing P by a holomorphic pair of sections of θ does not change [J]. The pole prescription is consistent under changes of compatible coordinates.
